title: Australian politics live: NSW One Nation leader clarifies anti-abortion comments; Joyce compares Hanson’s Indigenous comments with melon-gate
text: 18.47 EDT NSW One Nation leader clarifies abortion comments Penry Buckley The NSW One Nation leader and state election candidate, Mike Newman , has clarified comments he made in support of a bill to explicitly prohibit sex-selective abortions at a rally outside NSW parliament yesterday. Yesterday, speaking alongside anti-abortion activist Joanna Howe , Newman said: And what we want to say to those people in there, we want to support people who want to make sure that abortion rights, we want to stop it. We want to make sure that same-sex, sorry, abortion is stopped. We want to make sure that people have the right to life, and we will vote for you in favour of that. After Guardian Australian contacted Newman, he said that “One Nation policy is clear” and the party’s platform opposed late-term and sex-selective abortions, but did not advocate for an outright ban on abortions. There are already restrictions on sex-selection abortion for non-medical reasons in NSW, and the upper house voted to formally oppose the practice in 2019 when the state decriminalised abortion. title: Six green card holders in Texas charged in federal crackdown on illegal voting – US politics live
text: 18.06 EDT Six green card holders in Texas swept up in federal crackdown on illegal voting Earlier on Tuesday, Todd Blanche , the US attorney general, alerted reporters at the White House to stand by for what he called “a big development” in the federal crackdown on voting by non-citizens to be announced by Ryan Raybould , the US attorney for the Northern District of Texas. When it came, however, Raybould’s announcement , that his office had charged six lawful permanent residents and one undocumented immigrant for voting in federal elections over the past eight years, hardly lived up to the billing. While six of those charged cast ballots in the 2024 general election, the impact of their votes was almost immeasurably small, given that two of them cast provisional ballots that were not counted, and 11,388,670 other Texans voted in that election. Donald Trump , whose false claim that voting by non-citizens is rampant inspired the investigation, won the state by a margin of 1,558,347 votes over his nearest rival, Kamala Harris . Photograph: Omar Ashtawy/HL/Getty Images US foreign policy US set to deliver 2,000lb bombs to Israel as part of vast arms deal Powerful bombs prompted such concern about mass deaths in Gaza that Biden officials paused delivery two years ago Associated Press Tue 15 Sep 2026 20.05 EDT Last modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 20.31 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Trump administration is planning to deliver powerful 2,000lb bombs to Israel as part of an upcoming arms deal, weapons that prompted such concerns about the possibility of mass casualties in Gaza that the Biden administration paused their delivery two years ago. The $2.8bn package includes 40,000 bombs, made up of 20,000 MK-84s and 20,000 BLU-117s, according to two US officials and a person familiar with the plan who spoke on Tuesday on condition of anonymity to discuss the package, which is not yet final.
